knowledge.finding: When testing strong-form betting-market efficiency, normalized/no-vig probabilities are the appropriate probability input; regressions using raw inverse odds can be biased toward falsely accepting efficiency.
knowledge.guidance: Keep no-vig normalization as the default live benchmark and historical-calibration basis.

knowledge.finding: Major sports betting markets are generally highly informative and often efficient within transaction costs; statistical biases do not automatically imply profitable bets after vig.
knowledge.guidance: Treat market price as a strong prior, not an opponent to be ignored. Require multiple independent signals before overriding it.

knowledge.finding: Favorite-longshot bias is widespread, but its sign and magnitude vary by sport, market structure, and bookmaker. Longshots often have worse expected returns, but MLB/NHL and some U.S. side markets have historically shown reverse patterns.
knowledge.guidance: Never apply a universal favorite/longshot correction. Use sport/market-specific calibration.

knowledge.finding: Individual bookmakers can fail to incorporate information already present in competitors' odds; aggregated/market-best information can be more informative than a single book.
knowledge.guidance: Preserve line shopping and consensus/sharp benchmarking. Do not treat one book as the truth.

knowledge.finding: Line movement often improves forecast accuracy from opener to close because informed trading/news is incorporated, although specific markets and early-season regimes can retain biases.
knowledge.guidance: Use close/near-close as the strongest market benchmark and track whether Betting Edge recommendations beat it (CLV).

knowledge.finding: Detailed MLB line-movement research finds forecasts mostly reliable but some repeatable intraday movement inefficiencies; newer work extends evidence of negative autocorrelation in moneyline changes across MLB/NFL/NBA/NHL.
knowledge.guidance: Keep movement path, not just opener/closer, where timestamped data exist; test reversal/overreaction patterns in shadow mode.

knowledge.finding: NBA opening-to-closing spread moves historically improve forecast accuracy and tend to remove opening-line biases, consistent with informed trader influence.
knowledge.guidance: Treat meaningful late moves as information; price recommendations against the latest verified line rather than stale openers.

knowledge.finding: Decades of NFL spread research generally finds a highly efficient market, with many historical home/favorite/underdog anomalies shrinking or depending on transaction costs.
knowledge.guidance: Require strong matchup/news/price evidence; avoid generic home-dog/favorite systems without current validation.

knowledge.finding: A 2003-2016 study found division-rival games were less likely to see the home team cover and less likely to go over, with out-of-sample model results near 57% in selected strategies.
knowledge.guidance: Use divisional familiarity as a secondary feature and revalidate on recent seasons; do not hard-code 57%.

knowledge.finding: Historical NFL research found extreme-temperature acclimatization effects were not fully priced in a 1981-2004 sample.
knowledge.guidance: Weather must remain matchup-specific and current; use as a model input, not a fixed historical adjustment.

knowledge.finding: Recent work on NFL information asymmetry finds that the relationship between betting percentages and moves can carry information, but direction matters and simple majority-fade rules are not generally supported.
knowledge.guidance: Splits should be interpreted together with verified line movement, never alone.

knowledge.finding: Compared with NFL/NBA/MLB/soccer, recent peer-reviewed NHL-specific betting research is thinner; historical reverse-FLB findings should not be assumed to hold unchanged in modern multi-book markets.
knowledge.guidance: Our current NHL open-close and movement calibration remains genuinely useful rather than redundant.

knowledge.finding: A targeted search did not surface a substantial peer-reviewed CFL betting-market efficiency literature comparable to NFL/NBA/MLB. CFL remains a genuine local-calibration need.
knowledge.guidance: Continue CFL historical acquisition/calibration; NFL findings are context only, not transferable priors.

knowledge.finding: High-frequency/in-play markets can incorporate major news quickly, but behavioral mispricing around surprise events and near expiry can occur. Efficiency is not constant through time-to-event.
knowledge.guidance: Live bets require a separate model/error margin from pregame; never infer live fair value solely from pregame calibration.

knowledge.finding: For betting decisions, probability calibration is more relevant than raw classification accuracy because EV depends on the quality of probability estimates at quoted prices.
knowledge.guidance: Evaluate models/signals with calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and realized EV—not win percentage alone.

knowledge.finding: NFL research using more recent samples found statistical inefficiencies in substantial home underdogs and nonlinear total-line effects, but these are sample-dependent and may not survive modern pricing.
knowledge.guidance: Use as a candidate-feature prior only; current-era holdout testing is mandatory.

knowledge.finding: Research has found home-field pricing biases in nationally prominent NFL games and tested similar effects in NBA and MLB; home advantage is not a stable universal betting edge across sports.
knowledge.guidance: Model home advantage sport- and context-specifically; never use a universal home-team premium.

knowledge.finding: Conventional bookmaker-margin calculations can understate average bettor loss when margins vary by outcome probability; soccer and tennis evidence shows longshots can carry systematically higher effective margins.
knowledge.guidance: Do not assume equal-vig allocation when converting odds to fair probability. Compare multiple de-vig methods and calibrate by sport/book/price.

knowledge.finding: Discrete bookmaker odds grids can mechanically create favorite-longshot bias even without behavioral mispricing.
knowledge.guidance: Treat some apparent bias as market-structure/margin shape rather than true predictive error.

knowledge.finding: In-play prediction-market research finds mispricing can increase following surprising major events, particularly late shocks involving longshots.
knowledge.guidance: Live-event shocks deserve separate recalibration and uncertainty; do not extrapolate pregame fair probabilities mechanically after major state changes.

knowledge.finding: A 2026 sports prediction-market study using 23 million trades reports that calibration changes materially near expiry and that parlays become increasingly overpriced with leg count.
knowledge.guidance: Treat near-expiry/live exchange probabilities and parlays as distinct products; do not assume static calibration through time.

knowledge.finding: A 2026 study on ~90,000 football matches reports that bookmaker-aware odds-only probability transformations can outperform standard multiplicative, Shin, and Power conversions for many books.
knowledge.guidance: Benchmark our current no-vig method against multiple de-vig transforms rather than assuming multiplicative normalization is always best.

knowledge.finding: A 2026 review synthesizes behavioral, informational and structural explanations for favorite-longshot bias and proposes bookmaker hedging as an additional mechanism.
knowledge.guidance: Use FLB as a calibration phenomenon, not evidence of a single bettor-psychology mechanism.

knowledge.finding: Management Science research using NFL games and lines found no strong inefficiency but showed team abilities vary meaningfully week to week and market participants have more difficulty learning from noisy observations.
knowledge.guidance: Recent performance should be shrinkage-weighted rather than blindly extrapolated; noisy games should receive less influence in team-strength updates.

knowledge.finding: NBA betting experiments found model selection based on probability calibration produced much better betting results than selection based on classification accuracy.
knowledge.guidance: Optimize and evaluate Betting Edge probabilities using calibration, Brier/log loss, CLV and EV—not pick percentage.

knowledge.finding: Cross-sport work on NFL, NBA and MLB shows home-field betting effects are context dependent rather than universal.
knowledge.guidance: Home advantage belongs inside sport-specific matchup/fair-value models and should not become a generic historical boost.

knowledge.finding: NFL out-of-sample betting strategies based on apparent inefficiencies produced mixed persistence, and documented inefficiencies tended to dissipate over time.
knowledge.guidance: Every NFL anomaly gets a recency/holdout test. Published historical profitability is never assumed to survive.

knowledge.finding: A 1994-2000 NFL study found no conclusive evidence of general inefficiency after testing weak-form efficiency, power scores, stadium characteristics and alternative strategies.
knowledge.guidance: Objective matchup features must clear current-price thresholds; descriptive football knowledge alone is unlikely to produce durable edge.

knowledge.finding: A consolidated 2004 NFL study found only fairly weak evidence for a home-underdog bias and no significant returns from momentum strategies.
knowledge.guidance: Do not encode generic home-dog or momentum bonuses. Require current price and independent matchup support.

knowledge.finding: A practitioner analysis of 12,624 NFL player-prop bets across DraftKings, ESPN BET, BetMGM and Pinnacle found Pinnacle the sharpest of the four and found probability-conversion methods that account for favorite-longshot-shaped vig improved accuracy.
knowledge.guidance: Player props should use book-aware vig removal and sharp-book comparison when available. This is a design prior, not a production adjustment.

knowledge.finding: Targeted searches still surface far less peer-reviewed calibration/efficiency literature for NBA/NFL/NHL/MLB player props than for game-level sides, moneylines and totals.
knowledge.guidance: Props require local calibration, greater uncertainty margins, lineup/minutes/role modeling, and stricter price verification. Do not inherit confidence from game markets.

knowledge.finding: Recent sportsbook and league integrity cases demonstrate that low-volume individual player props can be unusually sensitive to private information and anomalous action.
knowledge.guidance: For obscure/low-liquidity props, increase uncertainty and require stronger multi-book confirmation. Treat abnormal market movement as information but also as an integrity-risk flag.

knowledge.finding: A second targeted literature search still did not identify a modern peer-reviewed boxing betting-market efficiency/calibration literature comparable with NFL, NHL, MLB, soccer, tennis or MMA.
knowledge.guidance: Boxing needs its own odds-history calibration. Fight-prediction models and pundit picks cannot substitute for market calibration.

knowledge.finding: CFL has legitimate in-game win-probability research, but targeted searches still reveal much thinner published pregame spread/moneyline/total efficiency literature than the NFL.
knowledge.guidance: Use CFL published live-model work as methodology, but build pregame calibration locally from historical CFL odds/results.

knowledge.finding: Research on COVID-era betting found unusual NBA moneyline inefficiency concentrated in specific underdog ranges, illustrating that structural breaks can temporarily invalidate normal calibration.
knowledge.guidance: Tag unusual eras/rule environments explicitly. Never pool structural-break periods into normal calibration without testing.

knowledge.finding: Recent prediction-market research finds apparent in-play arbitrage/mispricing can be real but fleeting and constrained by order-book depth and execution size.
knowledge.guidance: A theoretical live edge is not sufficient; Betting Edge should distinguish quoted edge from executable edge and consider liquidity/timing where relevant.

knowledge.finding: Levitt showed that sportsbooks need not simply balance equal money on both sides; bookmakers can exploit bettor biases and set prices strategically while managing exposure.
knowledge.guidance: Do not assume sportsbook prices are neutral forecasts plus symmetric vig. Book identity, clientele and shading can matter.

knowledge.finding: Shin developed a bookmaker-pricing model in which possible insider trading changes optimal odds and helps explain asymmetric margin allocation across outcomes.
knowledge.guidance: Supports comparing multiplicative no-vig with Shin-style de-vig rather than assuming equal proportional margin removal is always correct.

knowledge.finding: Forecasting research comparing prediction markets, betting odds and tipsters found market-based forecasts highly competitive with expert forecasts.
knowledge.guidance: Named handicappers and pundits should remain secondary contextual signals; market prices and independently measured information stay primary.

knowledge.finding: Classic NFL work reported evidence suggesting exploitable structure in point spreads, helping launch the subsequent efficiency debate and many replication studies.
knowledge.guidance: Historical NFL anomalies are useful hypothesis generators, but later research and edge decay mean they require modern holdouts.

knowledge.finding: A subsequent NFL study reexamined earlier claims of spread inefficiency and contributed to the broader conclusion that simple exploitable rules are fragile across samples and methods.
knowledge.guidance: Any NFL historical pattern needs independent replication and true holdout testing before receiving even shadow weight.

knowledge.topic: Player props: is there strong peer-reviewed calibration research?
knowledge.finding: Targeted searches still do not reveal a broad peer-reviewed player-prop efficiency literature comparable with sides/totals. Practitioner work suggests sharp-book comparison and non-uniform vig treatment matter, but this is not enough to establish production priors.
knowledge.guidance: Props stay local-calibration-first with larger model-error margins, strict book/price verification, lineup/role/minutes inputs and stronger sample requirements.

knowledge.topic: Live betting: should we assume prices incorporate new information instantly?
knowledge.finding: No. Peer-reviewed in-play soccer research finds both rapid efficiency and systematic short-lived mispricing depending on surprise. One study of 2,017 matches and ~£3B volume found expected goals were underreacted to while highly surprising goals were overreacted to, with effects fading over roughly five minutes. Other high-frequency work finds prices can update swiftly and fully around cleaner news events.
knowledge.guidance: Live analysis requires event-surprise/state-change logic and time-since-event. Do not treat pregame fair value or immediate post-event price as automatically correct.

knowledge.topic: Should live models be anchored to pregame market information?
knowledge.finding: Yes. Both CFL and modern in-play football modeling show that pregame market calibration is a dominant predictor of live win probability; current game state should update that strong prior rather than replace it.
knowledge.guidance: Live Betting Edge architecture should be prior + state update: pregame market probability, then score/time/possession or sport-specific state variables.

knowledge.topic: Can sportsbook line movement itself overreact?
knowledge.finding: Yes. Recent peer-reviewed work finds negative autocorrelation in moneyline changes across NFL, NBA and NHL from 2019-2023, extending earlier MLB intraday findings.
knowledge.guidance: Track sequences of moves and reversals, not just net open-to-current movement. A move can be information, overreaction, or both at different horizons.

knowledge.topic: Do statistical betting models need to maximize pick accuracy?
knowledge.finding: No. A 2024 published study using NBA betting experiments finds calibration-based model selection materially outperforms accuracy-based selection for wagering decisions.
knowledge.guidance: Use calibration/Brier/log loss/CLV/EV as core evaluation metrics. Win percentage is secondary.

knowledge.topic: Are player/micro props unusually sensitive to integrity risk?
knowledge.finding: Yes. Recent regulated-market actions and criminal cases show micro-props can be manipulated by a single participant without changing game outcome, leading MLB and sportsbooks to cap or restrict pitch-level wagers.
knowledge.guidance: Micro-props get a separate integrity-risk flag, reduced confidence, smaller allowable exposure, and stronger multi-book/movement scrutiny.

knowledge.finding: Broad peer-reviewed calibration research remains sparse. Practitioner NFL work over 12,624 prop bets finds book differences and favorite-longshot-shaped vig matter; a 2026 NBA thesis links FanDuel closing prop lines to player outcomes but is not a market-efficiency study.
knowledge.guidance: Own this locally: book-aware de-vig, lineup/role/minutes/usage inputs, higher model-error margin, and strict multi-book price checks.

knowledge.finding: Recent league/sportsbook integrity cases show participant-controlled micro outcomes can be manipulated or influenced by private information.
knowledge.guidance: Apply explicit integrity-risk penalty and smaller maximum exposure; avoid treating apparent line moves as purely predictive.

knowledge.finding: A 2025 peer-reviewed study of 2019-2023 moneyline movement across three sportsbooks finds significant negative autocorrelation in NFL, NBA and NHL price changes.
knowledge.guidance: Track movement path, reversal and time since move. Never assume 'more steam = more truth'.

knowledge.finding: Recent market-efficiency and expected-loss research shows proportional normalization can be biased when margin allocation varies with price; Shin and other transformations can be more appropriate in some markets.
knowledge.guidance: Use proportional no-vig as baseline, but benchmark Shin/power/book-aware methods before production historical adjustments.

knowledge.finding: Crossing football key numbers 3 and 7 can create large demand discontinuities without corresponding return predictability; meaningful quote changes are not automatically private-information signals.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Contest contract data are not identical to sportsbook inventory and the result applies to football spread thresholds.

knowledge.finding: Preseason expectations can remain associated with bettor behavior and sportsbook closing prices well into an NFL season; preseason anchors are therefore context, not independent current-value evidence.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Underlying data are not shareable and the study is game-market behavior rather than player-prop calibration.

knowledge.finding: Strong NFL player-stat mechanism evidence exists, but robust multi-book closing calibration for regulated passing, rushing, receiving and anytime-TD props remains insufficient.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Gap record; supports NR or caveated mechanism fit.

knowledge.finding: Major injury history can alter later participation and performance in position-dependent ways, so volume props should treat role and expected participation as uncertain inputs rather than applying one fixed injury penalty.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Long-horizon return-to-play study, not a same-week availability model and not sportsbook prop calibration.

knowledge.finding: Receiving props should separate target opportunity, catch probability, defender context and yardage distribution rather than treating rolling receptions or receiving yards as stationary.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Tracking/forecast mechanism evidence, not direct sportsbook prop calibration.

knowledge.finding: NFL bettors exhibit aggregate momentum behavior, especially in totals, but observed momentum behavior does not imply a robust current predictive edge and reported trading outcomes are mixed.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Older 2003–2017 market regime.

knowledge.finding: Online bookmaker price changes can reflect demand elasticity and order-flow shocks as well as information; movement alone should not be interpreted as a pure informed-money signal.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Broad microstructure evidence rather than a sport-specific predictive rule.

knowledge.finding: Parlay adoption rose sharply within bettors in a large regulated NFL wagering sample and higher parlay use was associated with higher sportsbook margins and bettor losses; multi-leg products require explicit margin/correlation caution.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: One sportsbook operator; does not establish a universal same-game-parlay correlation-pricing rule.

knowledge.finding: Modern retail betting markets are changing rapidly through technology, regulation and product design; historical priors require explicit market-regime transportability review.
knowledge.guidance: Apply only within the stated sport/market/timing scope. Preserve this limitation: Synthesis/context rather than independent predictive evidence.

knowledge.finding: Modern competitive fixed-odds markets can exhibit favorite-longshot bias even without a monopoly bookmaker. Whelan documents rising loss rates as implied win probability falls in 56,004 professional tennis matches, with especially poor outcomes for extreme longshots, and shows bettor disagreement plus bookmaker risk aversion can generate the pattern.
knowledge.guidance: Treat extreme long prices as requiring more, not less, independent support. Do not apply the tennis loss curve numerically across sports; use the result as a market-structure caution against treating a large payout or one-book outlier as evidence of value.

knowledge.finding: Across the Research Library, extreme-tail pricing, bookmaker risk aversion, order flow, liquidity and competitor-quote information all imply the same boundary: a large cross-book gap is evidence of price uncertainty/market structure, not an independent handicap signal. The longest quote can be useful execution only after a separately supported case exists.
knowledge.guidance: For History Fit, distinguish 'best price available' from 'independently supported value.' When the candidate case is only one-book outlier + no-vig residual + unresolved information, prefer caution/NR and do not describe the structure as near-actionable research support.
